basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 12.' and it opens '(Cap. XX.—Vers. 12.) Etenim vere soror mea est de patre, sed non ex matre. Id est,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XX.—Vers. 12.) Etenim vere soror mea est de patre, sed non ex matre. Id est, fratris ejus est Aran filia, non sororis. Sed quia in Hebraeo habet: vere soror mea est, filia patris mei, et non filia matris meae: et magis sonat, quod soror Abrahae fuerit, in excusationem ejus dicimus, necdum illo tempore tales nuptias lege prohibitas.
